title: The gangsters' night at Connie's Inn and the $200 tips
summary: The gangsters tip lavishly and behave like gentlemen; each man got $200.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So I heard, because other people had seen them, and even from where I lived, my folks could see these big cars out there. And they came in, and Alley -- he was the past grand master of that. He could cater to anybody, he knew just how to do it. And one of them would come in, they'd be dancing and we'd start playing and all like this.

And right away, before we had played hardly any time, the waiter came around with a tray for drinks. Drinks for us? One of the gang -- and I thought they'd all be guys with great big guns on them and everything. I had never been around any gangsters. They dressed like gentlemen. Of course, they had guns. I managed to see one gun one time, dancing around. He had it down in here.

There was guns there, but they acted like gentlemen. And tip? Oh, boy, did they tip. They come up to the bandstand and say, are you the leader? And I'd say, yes, I'm the leader, can I please you, anything you'd like? And, yes, do you mind playing such-and-such? Why, certainly. Okay, fellows, such-and-such a number, one, two, three, boom, and we knew it all and hit it just like that.

Guy would reach in his pocker and pull out a great big wad like that. (Unintelligible) to play that number. Sometimes it was 20, sometimes it was ten. And we had a kitty, had a box. Here's another one, fellows. We played all night long, because they hired the place, they could stay as late as
they pleased. And we didn't mind because we were getting tips. We were working, but those were tips. Lord, lord, lord.

When we got through that night, those guys -- every one of them had plenty of money. And there must have been 40, 50 of them. And they had plenty of money, they had plenty of girls. And they were dancing around, and liquor was flowing, and nice, wasn't any disturbance or anything. Everybody was laughing. And I thought to myself, now, all the time I've been reading about gangsters in books and things, and shooting and killing and everything. And I thought something was going to happen down there. They'd shoot somebody.

No, nothing like that. It was just nice as could be, just as nice, just as nice. And after it was all over, we counted up, and we had 11 men in the band, and each one of us got $200. Now, ain't that something?
That was a lot of money then?
I never made that many tips before in my life. Dutch Schultz. I had a $50 tip one time. The fellow didn't know it. __________ didn't know it, either.
